The discomfort may come from somewhere else. Give yourself a moment:

string-array.name: body_tips_food
string-array.item: Something simple is fine: fruit, nuts, a yoghurt or a piece of toast.
Even if you do not feel hungry, try something small: sometimes hunger only shows once you eat.
Better with some protein (egg, cheese, pulses, nuts): the dip takes longer to come back.
Leave something to eat in sight for next time.

string-array.name: body_tips_water
string-array.item: A full glass now, in sips.
Keep the bottle in sight: out of sight, out of mind.
If plain water bores you, try a few drops of lemon or a cold infusion.

string-array.name: body_tips_bathroom
string-array.item: Go now: holding it in also affects your mood even if you do not notice.
Take the chance to wash your face with cool water.

string-array.name: body_tips_sleep
string-array.item: With little sleep everything is twice as hard: lower the bar for today.
If you can, 10 or 20 minutes lying down with your eyes closed help even if you do not sleep.
Tonight, put the screen away a while before bed.
Today is not a good day for big decisions: note them down for tomorrow.

string-array.name: body_tips_senses
string-array.item: Find a quieter place, even for a few minutes.
Headphones or earplugs, even without music.
Turn down the screen and room lights.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly while you count five breaths.

resources.string: After a lot of stimulation, normal things feel boring or irritating. It is a passing dip, not your fault.

string-array.name: body_tips_crash
string-array.item: Move for 5 minutes: walk, stretch or dance to one song.
Get some daylight or look out of the window for a moment.
Put on music you like while you do something simple.
Do not go back to the same stimulus to escape it: swap it for something calm for a while.
Pick a small task with a clear end: wash a mug, make the bed.
Eat or drink something if it has been a while.
Tell someone you trust: \"I am in a dip for a bit, it is not about you\".
